overview: Magnification makes an image bigger; resolution determines whether making it bigger actually reveals more detail.
genZNote: Magnification: zooming in on a blurry photo. Resolution: whether zooming in actually shows you anything new.

aspects.label: Definition
aspects.valueA: The ability to distinguish two close objects as separate, distinct points.
aspects.valueB: The degree to which an image is enlarged compared to the actual object size.

aspects.label: What Limits It
aspects.valueA: Limited by the wavelength of light or electrons used.
aspects.valueB: Limited mainly by the optical/lens system's design — can be increased almost indefinitely.

aspects.label: Practical Effect
aspects.valueA: Determines the finest detail visible, regardless of zoom level.
aspects.valueB: Just makes the image bigger — zooming into a low-resolution image only produces a bigger, blurrier image ('empty magnification').

overlay.examHighYieldNote: 'Empty magnification' — increasing magnification beyond the microscope's resolution limit — is a classic exam trap testing whether students understand the difference.
overlay.memoryTrick: Magnification = how big. Resolution = how sharp/clear.
overlay.commonMisconception: Higher magnification does not automatically mean you're seeing more detail — without matching resolution, you just get a bigger blur.
